cause_plain: Building a link fails if a URL value is named "self". Python reads that value as the app object's own argument, so it crashes instead of adding it to the link.
real_cause: Flask.url_for() declared self as an ordinary parameter, so a URL value named 'self' passed via **values collided with it; the fix makes self positional-only.

cause_plain: A request to a web address with a path starting with two slashes, like http://site//v:h, crashed with a raw low-level error. The HTTP library read the path as a host and port, and "h" isn't a valid port. It should have told the caller the URL was invalid.
real_cause: HTTPAdapter.request_url() passed a path starting with '//' through unchanged, and urllib3 then parsed '//v:h' as a network location and failed; the fix collapses the leading slashes.

cause_plain: A POST that gets redirected (301, 302 or 303) is re-sent as a GET with no body. The old Content-Length header was copied onto it, so the client promised 5 bytes and sent none. The request failed and the real response was never read. Users saw a timeout or protocol error instead of the redirected page.
real_cause: RedirectMiddleware.redirect_headers() kept Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding when a redirect switched the method to GET and dropped the body, so h11 saw too little data for the declared length.

cause_plain: A template that outputs a number failed to render in Jinja's "native" mode. Somewhere, the number is being joined into text without being converted to a string first. I could not confirm which line does this, so this diagnosis is a guess.
real_cause: BlockReference.__call__/_async_call joined block output with the module-level str concat instead of environment.concat, so NativeEnvironment blocks returning non-strings failed.

cause_plain: The app crashes on startup, so users get no service. A route is declared with status 204 (No Content), but its function has a return type like `-> dict`. FastAPI treats that return type as a response body, and 204 responses can't have one.
real_cause: get_typed_annotation() turned the string annotation 'None' (from postponed annotations) into NoneType rather than None, so the route was treated as having a response body and the 204 assertion failed.

cause_plain: Black reformatted a piece of code and its own safety check found that the result was not valid Python. Black refused to output it and reported an internal error. I can't tell which input caused it.
real_cause: left_hand_split() only checked for a missing opening bracket, not for empty tail leaves, so at line length 1 it produced a split that broke the code and failed the equivalence check.

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a file that has a triple-quoted multiline string. It checked whether a line fits, and that check read a nesting-depth value that was never set on some pieces of the line.
real_cause: blib2to3 Leaf declared bracket_depth only as an annotation and neither __init__ nor clone() set it, so leaves created outside the bracket tracker lacked the attribute that is_line_short_enough() reads.

cause_plain: Loading data with `sentinel` set to null was rejected with 'Field may not be null.' I can't see a bug in the library code. This looks like the expected result for a field that doesn't allow null.
real_cause: fields.Constant set load_default/dump_default after Field.__init__ had already computed allow_none from a missing default, so a None constant was rejected as null on load.

cause_plain: A class that uses a `__attrs_pre_init__` hook with arguments and has a keyword-only field with a default value can't be created. The `@define` decorator fails with a SyntaxError when the app imports the module. The code attrs generates for that class is invalid Python.
real_cause: _attrs_to_init_script() built the __attrs_pre_init__ call from kw_only argument strings that still included '=default', generating invalid code like a=attr_dict['a'].default=a=....

cause_plain: Celery crashed with an empty-message TypeError while cleaning up a task result object that was being garbage-collected. This is most likely to happen when the app or interpreter is shutting down. The cleanup runs in a destructor, so the error is only printed as noise and the user's work isn't affected. I couldn't confirm the exact trigger.
real_cause: BaseKeyValueStoreBackend._get_key_for() passed the task id straight to key_t(), so a uuid.UUID task id made the bytes join raise TypeError.
